E13 fails the bar I set. It went from 13.67% to 12.89%, a change of -0.78 ± 1.11, with 3 answers going wrong to right and 5 right to wrong, so reading the problem more doesn't help in free generation at this strength. The uniform bias is closed as a candidate, and I'll drop it so the original stays the active submission; a copy remains in `cands`.

Two features of this pass could limit that conclusion, and both can be checked without spending a pass:
- **Few changed outcomes:** the standard error is well below the usual 2.7, which could mean few answers changed at all.
- **Low baseline:** `dev_a2` scored 13.7%, against about 21% overall, so this set may be hard and leave few right answers to lose or gain.

So I'll measure how many answers diverged and where, and whether coverage of needed problem numbers rose, since that was the failure E13 targeted. If coverage rose but accuracy didn't, wrong picks aren't what limits the model. If coverage didn't move, the edit never changed that behaviour in free-running text.

I'll also compare baseline accuracy across the earlier sets. And because the restart cut off the start of the notes, I'll reread the earliest closed lines before choosing how to use the 7 exploration passes left after the 4 reserved for HOLDOUT.

E13 did what it was built to do in free generation, but accuracy didn't follow:
- **The edit was active:** 147 of 256 answers diverged, and 98 of them changed their final answer.
- **Coverage rose:** among the diverged answers, coverage of needed problem numbers went up +1.6 ± 0.8 points, and answers missing a needed number fell from 24.6% to 20.4%.
- **Accuracy didn't:** on those same answers it went from 11.6% to 10.2%.

So making the model use more of the problem's numbers doesn't produce right answers. Missing numbers look like a symptom of a wrong plan rather than its cause, and I'm closing the reading-balance line.

One caveat is that `dev_a2` is a hard split, at 13.7% in both pass 17 and pass 39 against about 22% elsewhere. That weakens the accuracy read, but not the conclusion that coverage moved while accuracy stayed flat.

Before committing my last 7 exploration passes, I'll do two free things. First, reread the middle of my notes (passes 9 to 25), which the restart hid, so I don't repeat a closed line. Second, check the other big failure class I recorded, premature finishing (a final answer equal to an intermediate value of the reference), and whether E13 changed it.

The rest of the notes adds two more closed lines. Premature finishing turned out to be a trait of the Here mode, and E5 already removes most of it. Loop breaking was closed earlier without a pass: in-loop neurons rank smoothly, with no isolated component.

The weight scan sits inside block 30, a long analysis block whose first 1,300 characters are only text analysis. I'll print the part of that block that touches weights, to see whether the scan covered:
- the spectra,
- entry statistics,
- the norm weights and the per-head q/k norm weights,

If it only looked at norms, an undetected fault such as added noise, a rank cut, or a scaled or sign-flipped head or neuron is still possible. A deeper scan would then be the cheapest way to look for a large lever before spending passes.
